## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The verse shares extensive parallels across early Buddhist literature. SuttaCentral identifies a full Pali parallel in *Dhammapada* verse 325 (Dhp 325) [SuttaCentral]. Curated passage-level parallels are also identified in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan collections: chapter 29 of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (*Yugavarga*), its Tibetan counterpart (*Uv Kg* 29), the Chinese *Faju jing* (T 210.31), T 212.30, and the *Faji yaosong jing* (T 213.29) [SuttaCentral]. The text is additionally cited or referenced in two sections of the *Nettippakaraṇa*, namely the *Catubyūhahāravibhaṅga* (Ne 9) and the *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna* (Ne 37) [SuttaCentral]. In algorithmic text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus detects three matching internal Pali passages shared with the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, with the primary alignment covering segments §0.4–1.4 of this text against §3054_5–3058 of the commentary with a similarity score of 0.95, while finding no cross-language matches above threshold [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
